components.name: Primary Button

components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; font-family: 'Golos Text', system-ui, sans-serif; color: #1c2b1f; } .ds-field-label { font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.3; letter-spacing: 0.01em; } .ds-input { background: #fcfefc; color: #1c2b1f; font: 400 1rem/1.5 'Golos Text', system-ui, sans-serif; padding: 10px 12px; border: 1px solid #7e8a80; border-radius: 8px; transition: border-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #425244; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #2c4030; outline: 2px solid #2c4030; outline-offset: 2px; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-input { transition: none; } }

narrative.overview:
Mike looks like the portrait: a linen shirt, temple embroidery at the collar, a split gate and rice terraces behind him, already talking. The interface should feel like that meeting. Close, specific, in daylight. Density is a working cabinet, not a campaign page. Type does the hospitality. Color is the embroidery, used the way thread is used: a green word, a rust stitch, a gold prong, and a lot of quiet ground.

The ground is shade under the gate, not the shirt. A tourist reads this on a phone in late-afternoon sun. An admin reads it at a desk. Both need a light field with real contrast. Warmth stays in the mark, the rust action, and the words.

This system rejects the generic slate SaaS dashboard (Segoe UI, gray panels), the luxury Bali resort brochure (gold serif, infinity pool, barefoot-luxury copy), the travel-blog cream and sand template, the neon beach-club / nightlife promo, and the corporate real-estate CRM.
keyCharacteristics: One voice for the Telegram chat, the admin, and the partner cabinet
Daylight paper with a green cast; the linen shirt stays in the portrait
Temple green does ordinary work; rust appears once; gold is only the gate mark
Flat surfaces, a 1px stone line, a shadow only under a dialog
Fraunces for the stitched name and page titles; Golos Text for everything said
Short Russian labels that say what will happen

rules.name: The Not-the-Shirt Rule
rules.body: Linen Shirt (#e7cfb5) is the portrait. It is never a page, panel, input, or button fill. Warmth is carried by the mark, the rust action, and the serif. If a screen looks like a travel-blog cream and sand template, the background is wrong.

rules.name: The Embroidery Budget Rule
rules.body: Embroidery rust appears once per view, on the action that contacts a person or opens a place. Enter, save, and navigate are temple green. Two filled buttons in one row are prohibited.

rules.name: The One Gate Rule
rules.body: Thread gold is the candi mark and nothing else. No gold type, no gold buttons, no gold rules, no gold chart as the only highlight.

rules.name: The Stitch and Speech Rule
rules.body: Fraunces is the embroidery: the wordmark and page titles. Golos Text is the conversation: labels, tables, buttons, and body. Reversing them is prohibited.

rules.name: The Logo Lockup Rule
rules.body: The only all-caps setting is the wordmark: MIKE, then BALI GUIDE. Section titles, buttons, and nav are sentence case. No tracked uppercase eyebrow above a section.

rules.name: The Straight Stitch Rule
rules.body: Fraunces ships with wonk at 0 and softness at 20. A high-contrast fashion serif, a script, or a gold headline is the luxury brochure, and it is out.

rules.name: The Flat Gate Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat. Depth is a 1px gate line (#7e8a80). A shadow appears only under a dialog or a menu. If the shadow looks like a 2014 app, it is too dark and too tight: lighten it toward terrace ink at 14% and keep the blur at 32px.

dos: Do set the page to Warung Paper (#f3f8f4) and body text to Terrace Ink (#1c2b1f).
Do use Temple Green (#2c4030) for the wordmark, primary buttons, active nav, and the focus ring.
Do spend Embroidery Rust (#8a4520) once per view, on the action that contacts a person or opens a place.
Do keep panels flat, with a 1px Gate Line (#7e8a80) and 24px padding.
Do set Fraunces on the wordmark and page titles, and Golos Text on labels, tables, buttons, and body. Both with Cyrillic.
Do write button labels as a verb plus an object, in Russian, sentence case: "Сохранить партнёра", "Открыть карту".
Do pair every chart color with a text legend.
Do remove color and shadow transitions when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is set.
donts: Don't build the generic slate SaaS dashboard (Segoe UI, gray panels). No slate palette, no default sans as the brand face, no gray-on-gray tables.
Don't drift into a luxury Bali resort brochure: gold serif, infinity pool, barefoot-luxury copy. Thread gold is the 28px gate mark only.
Don't use the travel-blog cream and sand template. Linen Shirt (#e7cfb5) is never a background.
Don't use a neon beach-club / nightlife promo: no cyan, magenta, or purple chart series, no glow, no glass.
Don't look like a corporate real-estate CRM: no dense gray grids, no tiny uppercase headers, no side-stripe alerts.
Don't put two filled buttons in one row, or use Embroidery Thread (#b46432) for text.
Don't carry meaning by color alone. Errors need a sentence. Charts need a legend. Selected chips need a state.
Don't animate layout, bounce, or reveal content by hiding it until a class is added.
